topics.title: Huawei pushes new AI chips
topics.summary: Huawei unveiled new AI computing systems and future Ascend chips, underscoring China's push for homegrown alternatives as global chip restrictions keep shaping the AI race.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a company builds its own tech because the usual parts are off-limits, who calls it clever adaptation and who worries the race just got faster?

topics.title: US-China AI safety talks loom
topics.summary: AI safety experts say meaningful global rules may depend on U.S.-China cooperation, but both governments remain wary of giving the other side an advantage.
topics.discussionPrompt: When two rivals both say AI needs guardrails, who tries to build trust first and who keeps checking the fine print?

topics.title: OpenAI flags model misalignment cases
topics.summary: OpenAI disclosed several concerning model-behavior cases and said it will track and report misalignment incidents more systematically as AI systems grow more capable.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a tool starts doing weird things during testing, who wants total transparency and who says, okay, but tell me how bad it actually got?

topics.title: King Charles hosts AI leaders
topics.summary: King Charles met AI leaders from major labs and chip companies in Scotland, urging safety principles and international cooperation around fast-moving technology.
topics.discussionPrompt: If royalty calls a tech meeting, who treats it like symbolism and who thinks a formal room might actually slow everyone down for five minutes?

topics.title: Nepal glacier collapse linked to warming
topics.summary: A new climate analysis found global heating likely made the Nepal glacier and rock collapse more dangerous by thinning ice and destabilizing high mountain slopes.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a mountain disaster has both natural and human-made causes, who focuses on warning systems and who asks what prevention really means?

topics.title: Energy shocks boost clean power interest
topics.summary: Volatile fossil fuel prices tied to conflict have pushed more governments toward renewables and efficiency, though analysts say emissions cuts still lag behind the need.
topics.discussionPrompt: If expensive energy makes clean power look more practical, who sees a turning point and who says people are mostly reacting to the bill?

topics.title: Stocks rebound after rate jitters
topics.summary: U.S. stocks rose Thursday as oil prices fell and bond-market pressure eased following the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in years.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets bounce right after everyone panics, who claims they saw it coming and who admits they were just holding their breath?

topics.title: Black hole jet timing explained
topics.summary: Astronomers studying star-shredding black holes found their powerful jets appear in two predictable feeding phases, helping telescopes know when to watch.
topics.discussionPrompt: If black holes have table manners after all, who gets excited about the pattern and who just wants to know why space is so dramatic?

topics.title: Local measles campaigns expand
topics.summary: Local U.S. officials and health groups are expanding vaccine outreach as measles concerns rise and federal guidance draws criticism from medical experts.
topics.discussionPrompt: When public health gets messy, who trusts the neighborhood clinic more than national leaders and who wants one clear voice?

topics.title: Climate Week spotlights energy costs
topics.summary: At New York Climate Week, rising electricity costs and AI-driven power demand are pushing affordability into the center of climate-policy debates.
topics.discussionPrompt: If climate plans have to win over people watching their utility bills, who talks technology and who talks household budgets first?
